globe.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate an alternate chapter of the SAME Earth in reference, after a devastating long-past science-fiction war in space and on the ground. ONE planet globe, Africa-centered same geography and viewpoint, square framing, diameter 85-90% of frame, transparent background. Preserve Mercury-study painted continuous high-fidelity low-fi raster artwork, natural softly luminous Fujicolor-like material colour, left illumination, right side dimmer but legible. This world is badly wounded but NOT dying: human civilization is gone and conditions are no longer habitable to humans; nearly all large terrestrial animals have perished, but resilient life remains and begins recovering. Express through landscape only, no animals or humans shown. Most continents charcoal/ash-grey scorched stone, faded umber burn fields and pale weathered mineral scars. Recognizable real coastlines, substantial deep blue/slate oceans still present. Small scattered remnant forests in moist refugia: quiet natural dark sage-green pockets in Congo basin, Ethiopian/East African highlands, Madagascar and a few northern river valleys; restrained teal-green coastal plankton and shallow-water blooms as signs of marine recovery. Only a small fraction of land green, no restored lush continents, no alien purple ecology. Signs of ancient space war: a few collapsed circular base foundations and broken ring-segments from fallen megastructures embedded in land, barely discernible from orbit, sparse incomplete geometric traces with subtle metallic-grey material difference, tiny relative to continents. Place one small fractured ring foundation in central Sahara and another faint incomplete circular complex in western Asia; these should be tens of kilometres in apparent extent, never hundreds/thousands of kilometres. Retire reference's oversized central African arc: replace with much smaller faint ruins. Very sparse tiny impact pits and roughly tens-of-kilometres blast scars distributed in a few war-damaged regions; clustered scars read as gentle damaged texture, individual craters near resolution limit, NOT huge lunar bowls, repeated crater icons or planet-scale holes. Faint weathered reentry streaks and interrupted linear wreckage traces, almost lost in terrain, suggest conflict fought above this world. No orbiting debris layer or floating stations: all war remnants belong to surface so they can transfer into a ground atlas. Quiet deep-time aftermath, no active explosions, fires, smoke, lava, radioactive glow, neon, city lights or new civilization. Cloudless, no haze, atmosphere halo, stars, ships, rings around the planet, text or UI. Compose readable broad material shapes with selective detail, not photographic noise. Planet remains blue and alive, scarred and profoundly inhospitable to humans.

plate.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Make the matching unlit 2D surface plate of the EXACT Earth in reference: long after devastating science-fiction space war, widespread charred terrain and collapsed circular bases, small surviving forest refugia and marine ecology starting to recover. Human-uninhabitable but living world, no restored civilization. One opaque edge-to-edge rectangular 2:1 full-world equirectangular plate-carree colour/albedo atlas, ideally 2048 x 1024. Longitude -180 to +180 left to right, latitude +90 top to -90 bottom, equator halfway down, Greenwich centered. Americas left third, Africa and Europe central, Asia right, Australia lower right, Antarctic land/ice at bottom. Real Earth geography once only, appropriate equirectangular polar stretching, matching seamless Pacific antimeridian edges. Preserve reference's composition of material: warm ash-grey, charcoal and faded umber burnt continents with recognizable coastlines, cold deep petrol/slate blue oceans. Match pale northeastern Sahara swept scar, small broken grey circular base foundation in central Sahara, faint larger fragmented base in western/central Asia, tiny scattered weathered blast pits and reentry scars, subtle ruined linear foundations. These are orbital-scale details, sparse and weathered, not huge crater icons, continent-size cities or repeated geometric stamps. Keep eastern/central African small sage/forest green refugia, moist Congo pockets, Madagascar green patches, faint northern river-valley greenery, restrained coastal teal plankton/shallow-water recovery. Extend similar sparse old war marks and small surviving forests to moist American, east Asian and Australian refugia, most land still scorched and barren. No alien purple growth. Match reference's natural softly luminous Fujicolor-like colour and high-fidelity low-fi continuous painted raster style, broad composed material masses with selective mid-scale detail, no pixel grid or noisy photograph. Surface albedo ONLY: remove directional illumination, night hemisphere, terminator, specular highlights, limb darkening, vignette, cast shadows, atmospheric halo. Uniform neutral diffuse lighting across complete atlas, only differences of material colour. No clouds, haze, smoke, active fire, lava, neon, city lights, humans, animals, ships, orbiting wreckage, floating stations, giant machinery, space background, text, grid, labels, borders, padding, inset, transparency or globe silhouette. A damaged world with continuing life, not dying.
